searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — critique and twenty plus improvements the awtsmoos gives critique the strength of gevurah, so added light does not become added noise. awtsmoos.com should preserve what already works, then remove the weights that obscure the living choice. evidence that changes phase one phase one suspected that advanced search disclosure might be unwired. inspection disproved that suspicion: form.css imports form disclosure.css, searchapp.boot() initializes searchcontroldisclosure, and the controller moves the existing controls into a native element without changing ids. therefore search logic should remain intact unless runtime evidence later proves otherwise. improvements to the original plan 1. preserve searchcontroldisclosure.js; do not rebuild a behavior already modular and semantically sound. 2. treat the screenshot’s compact search options block as successful progressive disclosure, not the source of the remaining clutter. 3. focus first on page hierarchy , not search mode semantics. 4. reduce hero vertical dominance so the query and first result own more of the first viewport. 5. remove or demote duplicate assurance copy when metadata already proves provenance inside results. 6. keep one primary visual accent for the search action; do not let every border, badge, tab, and rail card glow equally. 7. keep scope navigation available but visually subordinate to the search task. 8. keep result status close to results, but make idle status quiet rather than another boxed panel. 9. keep query and results in the same dominant column at desktop widths. 10. reconsider the permanent desktop discovery rail; secondary context should not always consume 17–21rem of width. 11. prefer one compact context affordance that can reveal lanes/history/help instead of three always visible cards. 12. on medium widths, do not merely move the entire rail below results as two more large cards; reduce its default presence. 13. on phone widths, do not make secondary context an 86vw horizontal carousel by default; that creates another exploration surface before the user finishes reading results. 14. preserve the existing safe area bottom padding and horizontal scope navigation safeguards. 15. preserve 16px minimum form text, existing focus visible rings, and native details semantics. 16. keep loading/error/empty states explicit, but reduce decorative containment around ordinary status text. 17. keep existing search history behavior and lane discovery data; change prominence, not capability. 18. do not touch shared civilization token/base/component styles for a route local problem. 19. do not create a new global shell or global override in the first implementation wave. 20. do not modify dirty screenshot families while other agents are actively changing them. 21. treat short height desktop as a separate ergonomic case because the sticky form can otherwise consume disproportionate vertical space. 22. measure whether the current sticky form collides with shared shell/header height before deciding to retain stickiness. 23. keep url/deep link query state and mode semantics untouched unless runtime testing proves a defect. 24. preserve exact hebrew, tanach, and persisted library modes while changing only how secondary choices are presented. 25. preserve result provenance, coordinates, rank/score, and destination links; visual simplification must never erase trust data. 26. avoid rewriting js solely to toggle presentational panels when native html/css can express the same state accessibly. 27. prefer existing small css ownership files over one replacement stylesheet. 28. add no test files until the first implementation draft exists; then test the actual changed contract. revised problem statement sefarim is not primarily broken because it lacks progressive disclosure. it is visually overloaded because the route treats identity, assurances, navigation, search controls, result state, lane discovery, local history, and help as simultaneously important. the reconstruction must establish a dominant sequence: where am i? → what am i searching? → what did the library find? → what context do i want next? next action write the improved phase two architecture around a search first content sequence, then make a specific candidate file plan without yet approving production mutation.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — improved brainstorm the awtsmoos is one while the vessels are many; hierarchy should reveal unity without flattening every voice. awtsmoos.com becomes calmer when the seeker sees one path first, then chooses which secondary context to rejoice. search first architecture the route should read as four visual zones, in this order: 1. identity — compact title and one sentence proving what this search surface is. 2. task — query field, compact search options disclosure, primary search button. 3. answer — scope nav, result count/status, result list. 4. context — indexed lanes, local history, and guidance presented as secondary material. this preserves all capability while removing simultaneous visual competition. desktop shape collapse the hero into a compact masthead rather than a large landing page billboard. keep the search form near the top, but make stickiness conditional on viewport height/available shell space. give results the full primary reading width. move discovery/history/help below the dominant result region or into a compact secondary context strip/disclosure. do not reserve a permanent 17–21rem rail unless runtime evidence proves users need it during result reading. use borders only for structural grouping; ordinary status/help copy should not look like an equal strength card. tablet shape one result column first. search button may span the task width when necessary. secondary context appears after useful result content, not as a two card wall immediately after navigation. scope navigation remains horizontally safe when its labels no longer fit. phone shape one column task and results flow. keep search options as native disclosure. keep scope tabs horizontally scrollable without page overflow. replace the current large 86vw secondary context carousel with a simpler low prominence context section/disclosure so accidental horizontal swiping is not required to discover history/help. preserve safe area bottom padding, 16px form text, and generous tap targets. information weight primary query search button results current result/source state secondary scope tabs search options provenance assurances tertiary indexed lanes browser history tips/help tertiary information remains reachable and truthful but should not visually compete with the current search answer. behavioral preservation searchapp orchestration remains unchanged unless runtime testing reveals a defect. searchcontroldisclosure remains unchanged. existing search ids and url state remain unchanged. existing local history and lane discovery remain unchanged. exact destination/provenance behavior remains unchanged. no shared/global styles are changed in this wave. likely implementation strategy prefer a route local markup/css reconstruction. rewrite the whole entry file if dom grouping/order needs adjustment. rewrite only the css modules whose responsibilities actually change. do not touch search algorithm/controller modules merely for visual hierarchy. verification model after code draft desktop screenshot/dom metrics at approximately 1440×900. user screenshot like 430px phone width. tablet around 768px. short height desktop around 900×600. query deep link with ?q=space+travel&mode=library. search options disclosure open/closed. scope navigation, lane selection, history recall/clear. console/network/static resource checks. wider site strategy once the first clean route is repaired and proven, use it as the template for the audit discipline—not as a css template. continue through clean route families while recording active owned broken routes for later takeover rather than colliding with concurrent work. next action write the phase two specific candidate file plan, then perform the third critique with at least thirty additional improvements before approving any production files.
